primary_work.title: Towards Causal Representation Learning with Observable Sources as Auxiliaries

decision: NARROWED BEYOND OBSERVABLE-SOURCE AUXILIARY CRL — NOT ADOPTED
prior_art_boundary: using observed or extracted causal sources as auxiliary variables for CRL is existing work under the paper assumptions
selecting observable sources with a known latent graph to maximize conditional-independence recoverability is existing work
auxiliary-conditioned subspace recovery does not discover raw-language equivalence
supplied parser, entity, target, environment, or trajectory-derived variables must be treated as supervision or leakage rather than semantic discovery
task success and improved disentanglement cannot substitute for direct recovery of utterance and residual target partitions
counterexample: Two models related by an invertible transformation within an auxiliary-identified latent subspace and simultaneous relabeling of fine-grained target blocks, raw-utterance classes, denotation, language encoder, latent decoder, and policy preserve the complete observed-source-conditioned law, graph-implied conditional independences, selected auxiliary subset, flow objective, task metrics, and language-conditioned predictions while assigning different utterance equivalence relations and target semantics.
official_code_status: primary paper and algorithmic description verified; arXiv record does not list a paper-specific repository and title-based GitHub search did not identify an author-controlled official implementation
